assessment: The incumbent appears useful when assignments are stable: those 24 exports had seven-minute median handling, below the target, while overall course-set accuracy was 32/40 and median handling was 17 minutes. Assignment changes coincide with six affected exports, supporting investigation of week-specific selection but not establishing causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only explanation. Execution lasts seconds, whereas replacement delivery can take days. Observed isolation is encouraging but does not cover the unsampled split-course center. All proposed explanations remain hypotheses.

openings.claim: Using current instructor assignments for historical weeks may select the wrong courses; renamed courses may additionally cause either selection errors or coordinator recognition errors.
openings.delta: Distinguish actual membership errors from apparent omissions caused by changed labels before changing export selection.
openings.prediction: If temporal selection causes omissions, fabricated reassignment cases will disagree with agreed weekly membership even when labels are held constant. If renaming affects recognition only, participant membership will remain correct despite reported missing courses.
openings.probe: In private staging, compare current exports with coordinator-agreed expected membership for fabricated reassignment, rename, unchanged and split cases. Track course identity separately from labels and check center boundaries. Use the existing CSV schema and keep attendance entry active. Scope any resulting fix within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Expected weekly membership can be agreed explicitly.
Historical assignment data availability and correction effort remain unverified.

openings.claim: Does replacement delay primarily reflect request handling, and does it consume coordinator effort or only elapsed time?
openings.delta: Separate slow delivery from the handling-time target; faster execution alone may address neither.
openings.prediction: A request-handling bottleneck predicts long request-to-job-start intervals; repeated follow-up effort would connect that delay to coordinator handling time.
openings.probe: During the two short sessions, have consenting coordinators use fabricated exports and replacements. Record request, start, completion and receipt times plus active checking, follow-up and import minutes inside authorized workspaces; compare with existing logs.
assumptions: Request timestamps can be captured within the bounded effort.
